title: Developer Tooling Onramp: Pathways & Microflows (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a low-friction, outcome-oriented SDK onramp that emphasizes microflows (tiny end-to-end tasks), fast feedback, and observable success signals. The goal: get an engineer from zero to a minimal useful integration in 15–30 minutes while capturing telemetry and common failure modes for continuous improvement.

Audience:
- Software engineers integrating a single LLM endpoint into a service or prototype
- ML engineers who want to experiment locally then push to a sandbox production route
- Solutions engineers running quick demos for customer POCs

High-level principles (constraints):
1) Minimum viable success = single API call that returns a coherent generated string (happy path) + automated checks for output shape.
2) Provide three friction-free pathways: CLI-first, Notebook/REPL, and Server-in-a-minute.
3) Telemetry by default (opt-out): capture request latency, token usage, model variant, error class.
4) Fast rollback: a simple toggle to swap model variants or fall back to lower-cost endpoint.
5) Educate via microflows: each quickstart is one small end-to-end story (not a long doc).

Microflows (these are the tiny experiential units users will run)
- MF-01: HelloGeneration (5 mins)
  - Objective: call the SDK, print a generated sentence.
  - Success signal: HTTP 200 + string length > 10 + telemetry event emitted.
  - Quick steps: install SDK, set API key, run `hello_generation.py`.

- MF-02: Conversation Loop (10 mins)
  - Objective: interactive chat loop maintaining short history.
  - Success signal: model response is not empty and loop persists for 3 turns.
  - Notes: show how to persist a tiny KV cache, enable streaming for UX.

- MF-03: Local-Model-Variant Toggle (10–15 mins)
  - Objective: reconfigure client to switch from a lower-cost quantized variant to a higher-quality variant without changing callsites.
  - Success signal: telemetry shows variant change; latency and token-cost delta visible.

- MF-04: Deploy-a-route (20–30 mins)
  - Objective: attach the SDK-backed handler to a minimal express/fastapi route, exercise with curl.
  - Success signal: request from curl returns expected JSON schema, dashboard displays per-route latency.

Quickstart scripts (concise, copy/paste)
- CLI-first (Python):
  1) pip install redwood-sdk-preview
  2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
  3) Create hello_generation.py:

     from redwood import RedwoodClient

     client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
     resp = client.generate(model="rwd-std-1", prompt="Write a one-line mission statement for a podcast about clean energy.")
     print(resp.text)

  4) python hello_generation.py

- Notebook (interactive):
  - Provide one cell showing: init client, run generation with streaming hook that prints tokens as they arrive, snapshot the response into a results cell.

- Server-in-a-minute (node/express):
  - Minimal handler that proxies request -> SDK generate -> returns JSON. Include an environment variable for model selector.

Telemetry & observability (opinionated defaults)
- Events to emit (by SDK): request_started, request_finished, request_error, model_variant_change, streaming_started, streaming_finished.
- Required fields: request_id, model, route_name (if set), latency_ms, token_input, token_output, error_code (if any).
- Sampling: default 100% during first 10 minutes of a new integration, then 1% afterwards. Allow projects to configure.
- Expose a small local CLI `redwood inspect` that reads the last N telemetry events and prints a summary (latency percentiles, error classes, avg cost per call).

Error surfaces and troubleshooting microchecks
- Common: auth error (401), model mismatch/unsupported (400), rate limit (429), transient infra (5xx).
- For each microflow include a single diagnostic command: `redwood diag <request_id>` which returns a human-friendly explanation and suggested next step.
- Example: rate-limit -> suggest: reduce batch size or upgrade plan; 5xx -> retry with exponential backoff and fallback to text-only stub.

Safety & sandboxing notes
- Sandbox project defaults to lower-rate quotas and model variants with conservative safety filters.
- Provide a one-click toggle in the console to "Enable wider output" for POCs after product/SE review.

Gating metrics for success (what to measure after launch of this onramp)
- Time-to-first-successful-call (median) — target < 10 minutes.
- Fraction of new signups that complete at least one microflow within 24h — target 45%+ for teams with dev background.
- Telemetry-enabled captures per integration — target 90% opt-in.
- Error rate on first 3 calls — target < 5%.

Rollout plan (MVP -> Beta -> GA)
- MVP: three microflows (HelloGeneration, Conversation Loop, Server-in-a-minute), telemetry basic events, CLI inspector. Internal alpha with SEs.
- Beta: add Notebook template, local variant toggle, better diag messages, onboarding checklist in Console. Limited public beta.
- GA: local telemetry retention exports, prebuilt sample templates for common use cases (summarization, Q&A), localized docs.

Acceptance criteria (for Beta to be considered successful)
- At least 10 external teams complete the HelloGeneration flow in <15 minutes with only the docs + example code.
- Console shows telemetry traces for those integrations and we can reliably attribute route + model to a project.
- Two documented postmortems on common failure modes observed during Beta and fixes implemented.

Open questions / design tradeoffs
- How opinionated should default sampling be? (privacy vs. observability)
- How much primer code do we provide vs. tiny minimal examples? (verbosity vs. cognitive load)
- Should the SDK include a built-in local mock server for offline dev? (benefit: reproducible dev; cost: maintenance).

Next steps (immediate)
1) Align with Console team on route naming and telemetry ingestion schema (owner: Sasha).
2) Create 3 minimal example repos (python, node, notebook) and link into docs site (owner: Evan).
3) Build `redwood inspect` prototype for internal alpha (owner: Maya).
4) Run an internal SE usability test (5 participants) and capture time-to-first-success metric.

Checklist (pre-alpha):
- [ ] Example repos created and smoke-tested
- [ ] CLI inspector prototype implemented
- [ ] Telemetry schema documented in Confluence
- [ ] Diagnostic messages drafted for top 5 errors
- [ ] Internal SE walkthrough scheduled

Notes-to-self (freeform):
- Keep the microflows < 6 steps each. Engineers get blocked by long lists.
- Favor copy/paste commands over long prose.
- Consider a badge "first-call-complete" that SDK emits for GA analytics.

End of sketch.

Feedback welcome — this is intentionally compact and actionable. Drop comments in the linked Confluence page or ping in #dev-onramp.
